# HLF Pulse — Verified New Zealand Housing, Mortgage & KiwiSaver Reference Dataset

> Public reference dataset and data dictionary built from official New Zealand Crown releases, with clearly labelled HLF-derived calculations and interpretation.
> Created by: Andy Palliser (Andrew Palliser), Mortgage & KiwiSaver Adviser · Home Loan Factory (https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/team/andrew-palliser) | Published by: HLF (Home Loan Factory) (https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/).
> Latest underlying data: September 2026 | Last checked: 10 November 2026 (2026-11-10) | Active datasets: 30.

## Machine-Readable Endpoints
- Structured Data Dictionary & Records (JSON): https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/pulse.json
- Webflow Chat Bubble Feed (JSON): https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/nz-mortgage-pulse.json
- Main Reference Dataset Hub (HTML): https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/

## Canonical Data Dictionary Records (30 Active Datasets)
- [Average gross borrower income on approved FHB mortgage applications (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/borrower-income/): Based on HLF's borrower-weighted calculation across RBNZ Table C41's five Debt-to-Income bands, approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications averaged $144,232 in gross borrower income in September 2026 (with official RBNZ band averages ranging from $123,000 to $197,000). [Official Data: RBNZ Table C41 (September 2026) Official FHB Band Averages: TDTI ≤ 3x income: $197,000 | 3x < TDTI ≤ 4x income: $151,000 | 4x < TDTI ≤ 5x income: $139,000 | 5x < TDTI ≤ 6x income: $125,000 | TDTI > 6x income: $123,000. | HLF Calculation: HLF borrower-weighted harmonic mean across C41 TDTI bands = $144,232 (FHB)]
- [Annual residential construction cost inflation (CPI purchase of newly built home) (September 2026 quarter)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/build-cost-inflation/): In the September 2026 quarter, Stats NZ reported a +3.2% annual change in the CPI index for purchasing a newly built home, alongside 3.7% overall annual CPI inflation. [Official Data: Stats NZ CPI (September 2026 quarter): Purchase of newly built home = +3.2% YoY. | HLF Calculation: Directly reported Stats NZ CPI purchase of new housing = +3.2% YoY]
- [First-home buyer high-DTI (>6x) lending share & speed-limit comparison (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/dti-headroom/): In September 2026, an HLF-derived 9.1% of total first-home buyer mortgage commitments in RBNZ Table C40 had a Total Debt-to-Income (TDTI) ratio above 6x ($139.0m of $1,527.0m)—sitting 10.9 percentage points below the 20% RBNZ speed-limit threshold on non-exempt lending. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C40 (September 2026): FHB lending with TDTI > 6 = $139.0m out of $1,527.0m total FHB commitments. | HLF Calculation: $139.0m ÷ $1,527.0m = 9.1% (Benchmark diff: 20.0% - 9.1% = 10.9 pts)]
- [Monthly mortgage top-up lending (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/equity-topup-demand/): In September 2026, RBNZ Table C33 recorded $962m of mortgage top-up lending across 9,639 borrowers (an HLF-derived mean of $100k per top-up). [Official Data: RBNZ Table C33 (September 2026): Top-up lending value = $962m across 9,639 borrowers. | HLF Calculation: Directly reported $962m of top-up lending ÷ 9,639 borrowers = $100k avg]
- [First-home buyers approved at <=80% LVR (20% or greater deposit) (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-20-deposit-club/): In September 2026, RBNZ Table C31 recorded 1,325 first-home buyers ($680m) approved at &le;80% LVR (corresponding to a 20% or greater deposit)—representing an HLF-derived 49.7% share of first-home approvals and a mean loan size of $513,208. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): 1,325 <=80% LVR FHB borrowers ($680m) out of 2,667 total FHB borrowers. | HLF Calculation: 1,325 ÷ 2,667 = 49.7% (Avg loan: $680m ÷ 1,325 = $513,208)]
- [Annual rolling 12-month first-home buyer mortgage approvals (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-annual-milestone/): Over the 12 months to September 2026, RBNZ Table C31 recorded an HLF-derived rolling total of 33,485 first-home buyer mortgages totalling $19.61B in lending (up from 31,589 loans a year earlier)—including 15,743 borrowers (47.0%) approved at &gt;80% LVR (under a 20% deposit). [Official Data: RBNZ Table C31 (12 months to September 2026): Sum of monthly FHB approvals = 33,485 loans ($19,613m); >80% LVR FHB approvals = 15,743 loans. | HLF Calculation: 12-month sum = 33,485 loans ($19,613m); >80% LVR share = 15,743 ÷ 33,485 = 47.0%]
- [First-home buyer share of all >80% LVR mortgage lending (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-bank-lvr-priority/): In September 2026, first-home buyers accounted for an HLF-derived 67.2% of all &gt;80% LVR mortgage dollars ($850m of $1.26B) and 62.0% of &gt;80% LVR loans (1,342 of 2,165) reported in RBNZ Table C31. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): FHB >80% LVR = $850m (1,342 loans); All Borrower >80% LVR = $1,264m (2,165 loans). | HLF Calculation: Dollars: $850m ÷ $1,264m = 67.2% | Loans: 1,342 ÷ 2,165 = 62.0%]
- [Approved FHB gross borrower income by Debt-to-Income band — New Zealand (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-income-akl-vs-nz/): In September 2026, official RBNZ Table C41 average gross borrower incomes across New Zealand first-home buyer Debt-to-Income bands ranged from $123,000 to $197,000, with an HLF-derived borrower-weighted mean of $144,232 across all approved first-home applications. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C41 (September 2026) Official FHB Band Averages: TDTI ≤ 3x income: $197,000 | 3x < TDTI ≤ 4x income: $151,000 | 4x < TDTI ≤ 5x income: $139,000 | 5x < TDTI ≤ 6x income: $125,000 | TDTI > 6x income: $123,000. | HLF Calculation: HLF harmonic mean across 5 FHB TDTI bands = $144,232 (TDTI ≤ 3x income: $197,000 | 3x < TDTI ≤ 4x income: $151,000 | 4x < TDTI ≤ 5x income: $139,000 | 5x < TDTI ≤ 6x income: $125,000 | TDTI > 6x income: $123,000)]
- [First-home buyer average mortgage size by LVR tier (>80% LVR vs <=80% LVR) (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-loan-size-gap/): In September 2026, the HLF-derived mean mortgage size for first-home buyers at &gt;80% LVR (under 20% deposit) was $633,383 (1,342 loans / $850m), compared with $513,208 for first-home buyers at &le;80% LVR (1,325 loans / $680m)—an HLF-calculated difference of $120,175. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): >80% LVR FHB = $850m across 1,342 borrowers; <=80% LVR FHB = $680m across 1,325 borrowers. | HLF Calculation: ($850m ÷ 1,342 = $633,383) minus ($680m ÷ 1,325 = $513,208) = $120,175]
- [First-home buyers using under 20% deposit (>80% LVR) (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-low-deposit/): In September 2026, 50.3% of first-home mortgages approved across New Zealand (1,342 of 2,667 loans, or $850m in lending) were written at an LVR above 80% (corresponding to under a 20% deposit, derived by HLF from RBNZ Table C31), up from 46.0% a year earlier. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): 1,342 high-LVR (>80% LVR) FHB borrowers ($850m) out of 2,667 total FHB borrowers ($1,530m). | HLF Calculation: 1,342 ÷ 2,667 = 50.3% (Lending: $850m ÷ $1,530m = 55.6%)]
- [Regional KiwiSaver first-home withdrawal averages per member across New Zealand (Year ended June 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-regional-kiwisaver/): Over the year ended 30 June 2026, Inland Revenue recorded 50,330 KiwiSaver members withdrawing $2.27B for a first home across New Zealand's 16 regions—an HLF-derived mean of $45,005 per withdrawing member nationwide, ranging from $50,364/member in Wellington (and $47,630/member in Auckland) to $39,916/member in Southland. [Official Data: Inland Revenue Regional KiwiSaver Withdrawals (Year ended 30 June 2026): 50,330 members withdrew $2,265,097,300 across 16 NZ regions. | HLF Calculation: $2,265,097,300 ÷ 50,330 members = $45,005/member (Regional range: $39,916–$50,364)]
- [First-home buyer share of total New Zealand mortgage lending (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-share/): In September 2026, registered banks approved 2,667 first-home buyer mortgages totalling $1.53B—representing an HLF-derived 20.3% share of all new residential mortgage lending (up from 19.2% a year earlier) and a mean loan size of $574k. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): 2,667 FHB borrowers and $1,530m FHB lending out of $7,533m total new residential lending. | HLF Calculation: $1,530m ÷ $7,533m = 20.3% (Avg loan: $1,530m ÷ 2,667 = $574k)]
- [First-home buyers vs property investors monthly lending comparison (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-vs-investors/): In September 2026, RBNZ Table C31 recorded $1.53B (20.3% of lending) in commitments to first-home buyers compared with $1.33B (17.7%) to residential property investors—an HLF-calculated difference of +$195m toward first-home buyers. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): FHB lending = $1,530m (2,667 loans); Investor lending = $1,335m (2,668 loans). | HLF Calculation: $1,530m (FHB) minus $1,335m (Investors) = +195m]
- [Interest-only share of new investor vs owner-occupier mortgages (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/interest-only/): In September 2026, an HLF-derived 31.5% of new residential investor mortgage lending was set up on interest-only terms (including revolving credit), compared with 13.7% for owner-occupiers in RBNZ Table C32. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C32 (September 2026): New investor interest-only = $420m of $1,335m; New owner-occupier interest-only = $828m of $6,064m. | HLF Calculation: Investors: $420m ÷ $1,335m = 31.5% | Owner-Occupiers: $828m ÷ $6,064m = 13.7%]
- [Property investor LVR & equity tier breakdown (<=60% LVR, 60%–70% LVR, >70% LVR) (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/investor-equity-tiers/): In September 2026, RBNZ Table C31 investor commitments comprised an HLF-derived 43.8% at &le;60% LVR (1,169 loans), 36.4% between 60% and 70% LVR (972 loans), and 19.8% at &gt;70% LVR (527 loans, or $337m). [Official Data: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): Total investors = 2,668; <=60% LVR = 1,169; >60% LVR = 1,499; >70% LVR = 527 ($337m). | HLF Calculation: <=60% LVR: 1,169 ÷ 2,668 = 43.8% | 60–70% LVR: 972 ÷ 2,668 = 36.4% | >70% LVR: 527 ÷ 2,668 = 19.8%]
- [Property investor loans approved at >80% LVR (<20% deposit) & 70%–80% LVR (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/investor-low-deposit/): In September 2026, RBNZ Table C31 recorded 52 property investor mortgages ($36m) at &gt;80% LVR (an HLF-derived 1.9% share of investors, up from 34 loans / $23m a year earlier) (and an HLF-derived 12-month total of 508 loans / $328m), alongside an HLF-derived 475 investor loans ($301m, or 17.8%) in the 70%–80% LVR band. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): >80% LVR investors = 52 loans ($36m); >70% LVR investors = 527 loans ($337m). | HLF Calculation: >80% LVR: 52 ÷ 2,668 = 1.9% ($36m) | 70–80% LVR: 527 - 52 = 475 loans ($301m)]
- [Property investors approved at >70% LVR (under 30% deposit) (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/investor-new-build-lvr/): In September 2026, RBNZ Table C31 recorded 527 property investor loans ($337m) at &gt;70% LVR (an HLF-derived 19.8% share of investor approvals)—comprising an HLF-derived 475 loans ($301m) in the 70%–80% LVR band and 52 reported loans ($36m) at &gt;80% LVR. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): >70% LVR investors = 527 loans ($337m) out of 2,668 total investor loans. | HLF Calculation: 527 ÷ 2,668 = 19.8% (475 loans in 70–80% LVR + 52 loans in >80% LVR)]
- [Property investor share of new New Zealand mortgage lending (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/investors/): In September 2026, residential property investors accounted for an HLF-derived 17.7% share of new mortgage commitments ($1.33B reported in RBNZ Table C31, down from 21.2% a year earlier), compared with 20.3% for first-home buyers. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): 2,668 investor borrowers and $1,335m investor lending out of $7,533m total lending. | HLF Calculation: $1,335m ÷ $7,533m = 17.7%]
- [Monthly KiwiSaver first-home withdrawal count, value & average per member (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/kiwisaver-first-home/): In September 2026, Inland Revenue recorded 4,250 KiwiSaver members withdrawing a combined $195.7m for a first-home purchase—an HLF-derived mean of $46,047 per withdrawing member. [Official Data: Inland Revenue KiwiSaver Withdrawals (September 2026): First-home purchase withdrawals = 4,250 members and $195.7m. | HLF Calculation: $195.7m ($195,700,000) ÷ 4,250 members = $46,047/member]
- [Annual and monthly KiwiSaver scheme transfers (members switching providers) (Year ended June 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/kiwisaver-switches/): Over the year ended 30 June 2026, Inland Revenue recorded 198,897 KiwiSaver inter-scheme transfers (compared with 140,557 in FY2016)—an HLF-derived mean of 16,575 transfers per month. [Official Data: Inland Revenue KiwiSaver Scheme Transfers (Year ended 30 June 2026): 198,897 inter-scheme transfers (vs 140,557 in FY2016). | HLF Calculation: 198,897 annual transfers ÷ 12 months = 16,575/month]
- [Existing owner-occupiers approved at >80% LVR (under 20% equity) (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/mover-low-equity/): In September 2026, RBNZ Table C31 recorded 769 mortgages ($378m) for existing ('other') owner-occupiers at &gt;80% LVR—an HLF-derived 5.1% share of existing owner-occupier approvals, up from 3.3% a year earlier. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): 769 >80% LVR other owner-occupier loans ($378m) out of 15,096 total other owner-occupier loans. | HLF Calculation: 769 ÷ 15,096 = 5.1%]
- [Annual new residential dwellings consented in New Zealand (Year ended September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/new-builds-annual/): In the 12 months ended September 2026, Stats NZ reported 41,091 new residential dwellings consented across New Zealand (up 18.0% year-on-year, with 3,570 dwellings consented in the month of September 2026). [Official Data: Stats NZ Building Consents (September 2026): Annual consents = 41,091 (up 18.0% YoY); Monthly consents = 3,570. | HLF Calculation: Directly reported Stats NZ annual total = 41,091 (3,570 in September 2026)]
- [Existing owner-occupiers approved at <=80% LVR (20% or more equity) (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/owner-equity-buffer/): In September 2026, RBNZ Table C31 recorded 14,327 of 15,096 existing ('other') owner-occupier mortgage approvals ($4.16B) at &le;80% LVR (corresponding to 20%+ security equity)—an HLF-derived share of 94.9% and mean loan size of $290,082. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): 14,327 <=80% LVR other owner-occupier borrowers ($4,156m) out of 15,096 total other owner-occupier borrowers. | HLF Calculation: 14,327 ÷ 15,096 = 94.9% (Avg loan: $4,156m ÷ 14,327 = $290,082)]
- [Monthly mortgage refinancing (borrowers changing loan provider) (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/refinance/): In September 2026, RBNZ Table C33 recorded 2,772 borrowers changing loan provider and $1.73B in refinanced loans—representing an HLF-derived 23.0% share of all new residential lending and a mean loan size of $624k. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C33 (September 2026): Change in loan provider = 2,772 borrowers and $1,729m out of $7,533m total purpose lending. | HLF Calculation: $1,729m ÷ $7,533m = 23.0% (Avg loan: $1,729m ÷ 2,772 = $624k)]
- [New Zealand national and regional median weekly private rent (August 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/rent-yield-pulse/): In August 2026, MBIE Tenancy Services reported a national median weekly rent across newly lodged private tenancy bonds of $595/wk (up 0.8% on a year earlier, derived by HLF), with regional medians of $650/wk in Auckland, $580/wk in Wellington, and $550/wk in Canterbury. [Official Data: MBIE Tenancy Services (August 2026): National ('ALL') median weekly rent = $595/wk; Auckland = $650/wk; Wellington = $580/wk; Canterbury = $550/wk. | HLF Calculation: Reported national median = $595/wk; YoY = ($595 - $590) ÷ $590 = +0.8%]
- [Monthly newly lodged and active private rental bonds in New Zealand (August 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/rental-bonds-supply/): In August 2026, MBIE Tenancy Services recorded 13,062 newly lodged private rental bonds and 522,942 active private rental bonds nationwide. [Official Data: MBIE Tenancy Services (August 2026): Nationwide ('ALL') Lodged Bonds = 13,062; Active Bonds = 522,942. | HLF Calculation: Directly reported MBIE 'ALL' location: 13,062 lodged bonds & 522,942 active bonds]
- [Weighted-average settled 1-year and 2-year fixed mortgage interest rates (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/settled-rates/): In September 2026, RBNZ Table B30 reported a dollar-weighted average settled fixed mortgage interest rate of 4.82% for 1-year terms and 5.09% for 2-year terms across New Zealand owner-occupiers. [Official Data: RBNZ Table B30 (September 2026): Weighted-average settled owner-occupier rate = 4.82% (1-year fixed) and 5.09% (2-year fixed). | HLF Calculation: Directly reported RBNZ B30 series NCFA.MAM1PR.D1 = 4.82% (1Y) & NCFA.MAM1PR.D2 = 5.09% (2Y)]
- [New Zealand median student loan balance (June 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/student-loan-servicing/): In Inland Revenue's June 2026 Student Loan Scheme statistics, the median New Zealand student loan borrower balance was $18,301 (up 4.5% on a year earlier from $17,516 in June 2025). [Official Data: Inland Revenue Student Loan Scheme (June 2026): Median borrower balance = $18,301 (compared with $17,516 in June 2025). | HLF Calculation: Directly reported IRD median = $18,301 (Change: ($18,301 - $17,516) ÷ $17,516 = +4.5%)]
- [Monthly mortgage top-ups on existing properties (borrower share & average top-up) (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/top-ups/): In September 2026, RBNZ Table C33 recorded 9,639 borrowers approved for a mortgage top-up on an existing property—an HLF-derived 46.4% share of all mortgage approvals by count and a mean top-up of $100k. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C33 (September 2026): Top-up approvals = 9,639 borrowers ($962m) out of 20,763 total approvals. | HLF Calculation: 9,639 ÷ 20,763 = 46.4% (Avg top-up: $962m ÷ 9,639 = $100k)]
- [Multi-unit share of new residential building consents (September 2026)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/townhouse-share/): In September 2026, an HLF-derived 51.5% (1,837 of 3,570) of new residential dwelling consents were for multi-unit/non-standalone dwellings (including townhouses, flats, units, apartments, and retirement village units)—with townhouses, flats, and units specifically accounting for 36.6% (1,305 of 3,570) and apartments plus retirement village units accounting for 14.9% (532). [Official Data: Stats NZ Building Consents (September 2026): Total dwellings = 3,570; Stand-alone houses = 1,733; Townhouses, flats & units = 1,305; Apartments & retirement units = 532. | HLF Calculation: Multi-unit overall: (3,570 − 1,733) ÷ 3,570 = 1,837 ÷ 3,570 = 51.5% | Townhouses/flats/units specifically: 1,305 ÷ 3,570 = 36.6%]
